lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 136, for issue 132: the status bar shows the selection on the left, and the folder total on the right.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one thirty-six, for issue one thirty-two: the status bar shows the selection on the left, and the folder total on the right.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The status bar now has two parts, and the folder total on the right drops the word Total.
It starts when the selection changes: the view's idle update starts the status bar job.
The job now keeps the selection as a left text, and joins the folder total and free space into a right text.
The view stores the right text in a new property, under the same lock and job guard as the old one.
The window binds both properties to the status bar, so the right part follows the active tab or split pane.
The status bar gets a second label at its right edge, which ends with an ellipsis when it's cut.
A size handler gives the left label its full width first, and the right label only what is left.
So the bar shows the selection on the left and the folder's totals against the right edge.
Before, everything sat in one left-aligned line, so a long selection pushed the total and free space off the end.
GTK's status bar has one label; this PR adds a second and decides how the width is shared.
In a search, the view sets both texts itself: the found count goes right, a selected result goes left.
Only the job that is still current may store its texts, so an older, slower job can't overwrite a newer selection.
The left label is cut only when it alone is wider than the bar. Right-to-left languages get the mirror image.
This is the issue's example before: one line, with Total and the free space after the selection.
After: the selection on the left, and the total and free space on the right.
With nothing selected, the left is empty and the folder summary sits on the right.
In a narrow window the selection stays whole, and only the right part is cut short.
The right part uses a bar between folders and files with nothing selected, and a comma with a selection, as the issue planned.
The PR changes six source files, adds a test, updates the text of an older test, and adds this page and its narration.
To undo, revert the squash commit; nothing is stored, so the bar just goes back to one line.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The first commit was built, tested and audited in a cloud container; the later gap and review fixes are left to CI.
The work follows issue 132's example and approach, and builds on issue 74's always-shown totals.
lines.say: The work follows issue one thirty-two's example and approach, and builds on issue seventy-four's always-shown totals.

lines.caption: The new test checks the bar with nothing selected, and with one file selected.
It narrows the window with a long name selected, and fails if the window can't get narrow.
And it opens a second tab, to show the right part follows the active tab.
The build and install passed, and 26 of 27 tests passed; the new test failed only on a label that was too long.
lines.say: The build and install passed, and twenty-six of twenty-seven tests passed; the new test failed only on a label that was too long.

lines.caption: With the label fixed, the new test passed three runs out of three.
The screenshot audit needed three rounds; the third found all six shots right, so it said pass.
Its advice led to a 24 pixel gap between the two parts.
lines.say: Its advice led to a twenty-four pixel gap between the two parts.

lines.caption: Not run here: the gap and the review fixes, which CI checks, and split view, menu tips and right-to-left.
Before the first push, a fresh agent reviewed the branch at high: two fixes, three findings skipped.
Removing two new comments was kept; clearing the right part while loading was undone, because the issue forbids it.
The skipped ones: the two formats, kept as the issue says, the missing explainer, and test edits since committed.
CI's own review lands in the code review comment on the PR; its results weren't known yet.
Your own folders, window sizes and theme can only be seen once you install the next build.
The PR, the issue and CI's screenshots are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one; issue 133 runs next in the batch, but on its own.
lines.say: No open issue depends on this one; issue one thirty-three runs next in the batch, but on its own.

lines.caption: One idea for later: give the right part the same format with and without a selection.
The job would build the right text from the folder total in both cases, as it already does with a selection.
In short: the selection keeps the left, and the folder total and free space always sit on the right.
